items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: he was playing Bud Powell and Thelonious Monk and Horace Silver for me and those were players I just had not been exposed to

ctx.x: Marian was just, as she was for so many people, especially women players I think, you know a mentor, she always looked out after me and gave me opportunities. I heard her playing a little bit. My parents had some LPs with her on it when I was growing up. But

what really turned the corner for me I think was when I got to study with John Mehegan, who lived one or two towns away from me in Connecticut. And I walked in there and suddenly there’s a lot of music for which I had no real true cultural reference. I mean he was playing Bud Powell and Thelonious Monk and Horace Silver for me and those were players I just had not been exposed to, and, but he was also playing Bill Evans and Herbie. And the first player I think to resonate with me the most closely was Bill Evans,…
About what years was — this occurred?
